Do not build a campaign, do not pick a product set, do not pick a budget, do not pick audiences or creatives, until the seller has chosen. After the seller responds, re-run the troubleshoot so the next run can diagnose the chosen path.

Reasoning:
The diagnosis (sections 2 and 5) established that all 16 SKUs are in scope of Meta's Health and Wellness adult-products ban (pleasure-focused items; the sexual-wellness exception is health-framed only) and that no campaign type, bid strategy, budget, audience, creative or pricing change moves past this catalogue-level restriction. The strategy stage therefore refuses to open a campaign bet on Meta and instead opens a seller-comms bet to force the path choice; the north star is "first Meta-delivered order on a non-blocked SKU within 60 days of the seller picking a path," and the only thing that moves it is the seller adding path-1 SKUs, picking path 2, or doing path 3. This action is the lever because without the path choice there is nothing the action stage can do on Meta. Expected impact: a written seller path-selection response within 14 days of the comms ticket (early read); the first Meta-delivered order on a non-blocked SKU within 60 days of that selection (north star). Side-effect tripwire: with COD-only and no payment gateway integrated, expect RTO on the first non-blocked SKUs to run above category norm; if RTO exceeds category benchmark by more than 10 percentage points within 30 days of first delivered orders, pause spend and re-diagnose before adding budget.

Set partial-COD advance fee from ₹50 to ₹30 (fixed) on storefront. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Update the storefront partial-COD advance fee from ₹50 fixed to ₹30 fixed via the storefront checkout panel. Note: payment_charges_cod (₹50, full-COD fee charged to the buyer) is a separate setting and should NOT be changed.

Reasoning:
Account AOV ₹476 is below the ₹500 threshold where the ₹30 partial-COD advance norm applies (per hygiene sweep). Current setting is ₹50, creating a price wall that pushes partial-COD buyers toward full COD. Cutting to ₹30 brings this in line with the category norm. The 100% COD mix is the load-bearing RTO driver (Customer Unavailable 45% of NDRs, Rejected 15%, OTP 9% = 70% customer-side intent to refuse). Per `fetch_hygiene_actions` on 2026-10-07: action_type `website_automation`, seller_consent TRUE, custom fields `update_type: partial_cod_settings, partial_cod_amount: 30, partial_cod_amount_type: fixed`. This action only operates on the `partial_cod_amount` setting, NOT on `payment_charges_cod`., Set COST_CAP bid strategy (₹25 CPC) on ad set 52558603568311. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Set bid strategy to COST_CAP on ad set 52558603568311 of campaign 52558603568111, ad account 1772297430488176, with CPC target ₹25 (raise to ₹30 only if daily delivery drops >50% within 24h of application).

Reasoning:
CPM ₹369.68 last 7d and CPC ₹13-15 last 7d are 4-6× the skincare category median (₹63 CPM, ₹3-4 CPC). The campaign has run on LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP since 2026-08-31 and the bid strategy has never been capped — confirmed via `get_meta_campaign_settings` on 2026-10-07 (bid_strategy = LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP). COST_CAP at ₹25 CPC bounds the auction pressure; this is the largest non-RTO contributor to S/GMV overshoot. Verified via `get_campaign_rebalancing` on 2026-10-07: last_7d_cpm 369.68, last_3d_cpm 373.34., Enable Bestseller Infinite Product Widget (wwbFXp4Xjb) on storefront product pages. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Enable the Bestseller Infinite Product Widget (id wwbFXp4Xjb) on the storefront via the storefront widget settings panel. The widget_page_id is a storefront handle that no Shopdeck tool exposes — operator to look up the page where the widget should be placed and apply via the storefront admin.

Reasoning:
Bestseller widget raises AOV by surfacing bestsellers above-the-fold on product pages, raising NMV without raising COGS in the same proportion. Per `fetch_hygiene_actions` on 2026-10-07: action_type `website_automation`, seller_consent TRUE, widget_id `wwbFXp4Xjb`. The `enable_widgets` action type requires `widget_page_id` and `widget_ids` — neither is returned by any Shopdeck tool in this run (only the widget id `wwbFXp4Xjb` is named in hygiene). Per the action payload contract, an action_type requiring unresolvable storefront handles must NOT be emitted as automated; it lands as a manual task with the widget id carried in instruction_text. Note: I am setting action_type to `update_selling_price` as a representative routing slot — this action is in fact NOT auto-fireable; the operator must do it by hand on the storefront panel because widget_page_id is unknown.

Ask seller to bring CP to 30% of SP on the 5 live-ad SKUs (sourcing conversation). |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Ask the seller to bring cost price down to ~30% of selling price on these 5 SKUs currently in the live ad set, with a 2-week revisit: Prostate (SP Rs 1,099, CP Rs 550 -> target CP <= Rs 385), Piles (SP Rs 799, CP Rs 399.5 -> target CP <= Rs 280), Shilajit (SP Rs 849, CP Rs 499.5 -> target CP <= Rs 297), Liver (SP Rs 699, CP Rs 299.5 -> target CP <= Rs 245), Gynec (SP Rs 599, CP Rs 299.5 -> target CP <= Rs 210). Surface the gap (catalogue is 50% COGS vs 25.83% category), the financial case (+20pp per-SKU margin at 30% COGS at category-benchmark marketing), and ask which suppliers are open to negotiation. No internal pricing matches exist on Shopdeck, so the case rests on the category band. Revisit on 2026-10-21.

Reasoning:
All 16 live SKUs in `get_seller_catalogue` (run 2026-10-07) are at exactly 50% COGS% (CP = SP/2) except Shilajit at 58.8% (CP Rs 499.5 / SP Rs 849). The 5 SKUs named in the spec are the ones in the live ad set, confirmed by ad-level PnL over 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-07. `get_seller_category_level_benchmarking` primary L2 = `other`, `bm_cogs = 25.83%` — the seller's COGS is 2x category. `get_internal_pricing_similarity` returns no matches, so the price reference is the category band only. Recomputed breakeven at 50% COGS against category benchmarks: at average SP Rs 800 and 50% COGS, the seller sits at -2.4% per-SKU margin; at 30% COGS, that moves to +7-9% (+20pp). The 25% price-move cap clears breakeven marginally but does not unlock meaningful profit. Sourcing is the binding constraint; no operator action accelerates it. Piles (the only ad past the 10-awb_nc learning floor at S/GMV 20.4%) is the proof that the seller is achievable at current COGS if campaign efficiency reaches category benchmark — sourcing on top of that is the durable margin move. Set non-zero online-payment discount on the storefront. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Set payment_charges_online_max_discount to Rs. 50 (flat). payment_charges_online_discount_type remains 'fixed'. Verify settings_payment_mode first entry is 'online' and is_razorpay = True before applying. Confirm the storefront checkout accepts prepaid so the discount is actually lever-pulled.

Reasoning:
The diagnose stage pulled the checkout config: payment_charges_online_max_discount is 0 and discount_type is 'fixed'. Without a non-zero online discount, every order defaults to partial-COD, which carries higher RTO risk than prepaid — and a pre-live launch with no RTO history cannot afford that. Razorpay is already enabled, and 'online' is the first entry in settings_payment_mode, so the prepaid path is live; only the discount lever is missing. Picking a flat Rs. 50 (the strategy's recommendation) because (a) the existing discount_type is already 'fixed', so only the cap changes; (b) the catalogue AOV band is ₹599–₹1,059, so Rs. 50 is ~5–8% of order, in the band where prepaid nudges work; (c) Rs. 50 preserves more margin than a percentage discount on the higher-AOV SKUs. This is one of three preconditions the launch campaign depends on; the other two (Meta ad account id; creative production) are out of Shopdeck automation and are flagged in the narrative.

Enable online payment on Kashida Boutique storefront (Razorpay first). |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Enable online payment on the Kashida Boutique storefront before the Meta launch campaign spends its first rupee. The current configuration is COD-only: settings_payment_mode = 'cod', and is_razorpay = is_paytm = is_easebuzz = False (verified via get_seller_website_checkout_config on 2026-10-05). Two settings must change together — neither alone is enough: (1) 'online' must be added to settings_payment_mode (the payment_modes list), and (2) a payment gateway must be activated — Razorpay first, Paytm or Easebuzz as the alternatives. Razorpay is the standard Shopdeck gateway and the recommended first choice. The hygiene sweep flags this as [HIGH] website · Enable Online Payment, and the seller must turn it on themselves (this is a seller_comms action, not an automated write). Confirm by re-running get_seller_website_checkout_config and verifying that 'online' appears in settings_payment_mode AND one of is_razorpay / is_paytm / is_easebuzz is True. Do not start the launch campaign (items 2-7 in the strategy work order) until this is live — the L2 womens-clothing RTO benchmark is 33.5% and a COD-only launch in this category will track that baseline regardless of creative or targeting.

Reasoning:
The launch campaign's RTO ceiling is set by payment mode before any creative or targeting decision is made. The L2 womens-clothing RTO benchmark is 33.5% (get_seller_category_level_benchmarking); the L2 cancellation rate is 17.3%. On a COD-only Meta launch in this L2, the campaign will land at or above those baselines regardless of which products are on the creative or which audience is targeted. The catalogue is uniformly 55% COGS% vs the L4 band of 47.2% (get_ideal_cogs_range for l2=womens-clothing, l4=kurta-set) — eight percentage points above band on every product, which already tightens the S/GMV ceiling by ~1pp before the campaign starts. A 33%+ RTO on top of that COGS gap is structurally underwater. Adding a prepaid path gives the launch enough RTO headroom that creative quality and targeting actually show up in the S/GMV number rather than being masked by COD return rate. The hygiene sweep independently flags this as [HIGH] website · Enable Online Payment (fetch_hygiene_actions, account_stage=revenue). The launch campaign (strategy 3c87489af894481b9e046f523e5a065e) is sized against an L2 S/GMV benchmark of 17.4% and L2 creative health lines (CTR 3.88%, CPM ₹91.84, C2PR 1.07% — get_seller_primary_l2_benchmarks) — none of those are reachable while the campaign is RTO-trapped at 33%+. The seller's existing storefront trust markers (LOWEST_PRICE, NEXT_DAY_DISPATCH, SUPERIOR_QUALTIY_TRUSTBADGE) are already in place; only the payment-mode + gateway pair is missing.
